title: SRing: A Sub-Ring Construction Method for Application-Specific Wavelength-Routed Optical NoCs
problem: Wavelength-routed optical ring routers lack customization for application-specific requirements, resulting in high propagation loss from long worst-case signal paths and excessive splitter usage in power distribution networks (PDNs).
motivation: Generic ring NoC designs waste power and area; application-specific customization can exploit communication patterns to improve efficiency.
method: This method breaks the single-ring topology into multiple smaller sub-rings connected by waveguides, greatly reducing the longest distance any light signal must travel. It then uses mathematical optimization—specifically mixed integer linear programming (MILP)—to determine which wavelengths (colors of light) to assign to each connection. This wavelength assignment minimizes the number of optical splitters (devices that distribute light signals) needed in the power distribution network.
key_novelty: Sub-ring clustering (dividing the ring into smaller interconnected sub-rings) combined with MILP-based wavelength assignment enables customization of optical network design for specific applications.
contributions: MILP formulation for wavelength assignment minimizing PDN splitters
Significant reduction in longest signal path length
Lower worst-case insertion loss and reduced power distribution overhead

metrics.other: Reduced insertion loss, reduced splitter count, shorter signal paths

baselines: Three state-of-the-art ring router design methods
limitations: Evaluation on six test applications; generalization to diverse application communication patterns and larger network scales unclear.
primary_theme: Application-customized optical NoC design via sub-ring clustering
